But now he's insisting on Thor, and if people don't, he cuts ties. I'm not used to it yet, and I'm worried about how he'll react when I try to switch. First, I need to understand why he's making this change. He mentioned that Thor is his Icelandic name, and maybe he's reconnecting with his heritage or identity. That makes sense, and I should respect that. But it's hard because we've known each other so long, and Tim has always been his name to me. I'm also thinking about how he's a hot-headed person. If I mess up and call him Tim by accident, he might get upset. I don't want to lose a long-term friend over something like this, but I also don't want to make him uncomfortable by not respecting his wishes. I wonder if there's a way to transition smoothly. Maybe I can practice calling him Thor in my head before we meet. Or perhaps I can ask him for some tips on how to adjust without making it awkward. But I'm not sure if he'll be open to that. Another thought is whether this is a bigger issue than just a name. Maybe he's going through some changes, and this is part of that. I should consider being supportive, even if it's difficult for me. But I also need to take care of myself and not feel pressured to change who I am. I'm also thinking about how other friends are handling this. If they're all switching to Thor, maybe it's easier for me to do the same. But I don't want to feel like I'm just following the crowd without understanding why. In the end, I think the key is respect. If he's made it clear that Thor is his preferred name, I should make an effort to use it. It might take some time, but showing that I care about his identity is important. Even if I slip up sometimes, as long as I'm making the effort, that should matter to him.
